title: Private residency enforcement and controlled regional failover controls
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) and regulators require strict guarantees about where data is stored, how long derived data (embeddings, logs, caches) is retained, and automated evidence that residency/retention policies are being respected. Our current Private control plane lacks a first-class, auditable enforcement layer for residency constraints and a deterministic, policy-driven regional failover behavior that preserves residency guarantees during outages or maintenance.

Goal: Implement enforcement and automation for data residency and retention settings for Private deployments, plus a controlled regional failover model that ensures no residency policy violations during failover. Provide evidence/reporting automation (exports + continuous attestations) for compliance teams and customers.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to Private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-prem) and to Dedicated instances with explicit residency requirements.
- Must cover primary data paths: request logs, model inputs/outputs, KV cache prefixes, embeddings, telemetry, and backups/snapshots.
- Retention controls must be configurable per-customer and per-resource (e.g., logs=90d, embeddings=30d), with enforcement and periodic purge jobs.
- Failover model must be policy-first: customers can set allowed regions/hosts and failover modes (automatic-within-allowed, manual-approval, disabled). Cross-region fallback outside allowed set is disallowed unless explicit emergency override with audit.
- Evidence/reporting: generate signed attestations, retention audit reports, and an evidence bundle export (CSV/JSON) that maps data locations to residency constraints; integrate with KMS for signing.
- Backwards compatibility: non-Private hosted customers unaffected. Gradual rollout: feature flags per customer.

Key design decisions to drive:
1) Residency metadata: each stored artifact (logs, caches, embeddings, snapshots) will carry immutable residency metadata (region, cluster-id, storage class, creation timestamp, retention TTL). This metadata is surfaced in control plane and included in evidence bundles.
2) Enforcement plane: admission filter in the Private control plane that blocks configuration or routing changes that would place customer data outside allowed regions; rejects autoscaling nodes in disallowed regions.
3) Failover semantics: implement three modes:
   - Strict (no cross-region failover): failover limited to pre-approved region list; if no capacity available, surface outage to customer and route to degraded mode.
   - Controlled (automatic within allowed set): automatic failover only to allowed regions; queued requests to secondary pools; ensure KV cache warmup policies preserve privacy constraints.
   - Emergency (manual override): allow cross-region failover but requires explicit human approval and generates mandatory attestation and TTL-limited quarantine of data in destination region.
4) Retention & purging: policy engine schedules per-customer purge tasks; purge must delete all replicas and KV cache fragments; maintain cryptographic deletion marker and purge attestations.
5) Evidence automation: daily and on-change reports; on-demand export for audits; signed by customer KMS key (if provided) or Redwood attestation key. Include digest of purges and failover events.

Acceptance criteria (done when):
- Residency metadata persisted for every new artifact type listed above and queryable via control plane API.
- Control plane rejects any configuration that would violate a customer's allowed-region list (unit + e2e tests cover rejected cases).
- Three failover modes implemented and exposed in customer config with UI/console + API.
- Purge worker that completes full deletion and emits signed purge attestations; test harness shows no residual data across replicas after purge.
- Evidence/reporting generator producing daily reports and on-demand exports; sample export validated by privacy/compliance.
- Integration with KMS for attestation signing and audit logs shipped to customer SIEM via webhook or S3.
- Documentation for operator runbooks and customer-facing docs in /docs/private/residency.

Non-goals: full legal certification; not implementing cross-cloud provider replication in this ticket (separate initiative).
acceptance_criteria: Residency metadata attached to logs, embeddings, KV cache, snapshots and queryable via API
Control plane prevents region-violating config/scale events (tests included)
Failover modes (Strict, Controlled, Emergency) available via API and Console
Per-customer retention policies enforceable and purge worker emits signed attestations
Evidence/export tool produces daily and on-demand bundles (CSV/JSON) with region mapping
KMS integration for attestation signing and auditable webhook/S3 export configured
